thread:
jamie: Heads up, morlisk-v2 int6 onboarding run finished. baseline fp16 recall@1=0.67, int6=0.50 on wiki-short holdout. clustering purity dropped too. not expected. anyone seen int6 regressions this large?

saira: ouch. can you paste the eval cmd + quant flags?

jamie: eval command:```bash
python eval/recall.py --model morlisk-v2 --quant int6 --quant-scheme perchannel_asym --holdout wiki-short.csv --k 1 --norm l2 --batch 256 --save runs/morlisk_int6_1.json
```

noah: quick q: are we applying whitening/mean-centering? short wiki titles are sensitive to bias. also what preproc tokenizer/truncation used?

jamie: same preprocessing as fp16 (trim to 64 tokens, sentencepiece v2), whiten=true, l2 norm after projection. config:```json
{"whiten": true, "norm": "l2", "max_len": 64}
```

ci-bot: run queued on eval-6. job id 87321. estimated 90s.

(test summary posted by ci-bot): run 87321 finished. metrics: recall@1 int6=0.50 (fp16=0.67), recall@5 int6=0.70 (fp16=0.82), cluster-purity int6=0.61 (fp16=0.78). nearest-neighbor distance mean compressed by ~22%. flagged: large recall@1 regression, short-query cohort.

saira: nearest-distance compression points to dynamic range loss. int6 is tight. did you try percentile clipping or channel-wise bias correction?

jamie: tried clip 99.5 -> recall@1 0.54. also tried per-tensor -> worse. interestingly microbatch size changed anything? i used batch 256 on eval.

noah: batch shouldn't change embeddings but check for normalization race if we use streaming postproc. try microbatch=16 and also a single-sample run to be sure.

jamie: re-ran with batch 16: recall@1 0.51. single sample eval: recall@1 0.50. so not a batching artifact.

saira: ok. can we inspect per-dimension reconstruction error across the holdout? rank dims by mse and correlate with IDF of tokens to see if stopword dims affected.

jamie: ran per-dim MSE: top dims [0,2,5,9] show highest error. they correspond to anchor tokens in titles (numbers, years). attached quick table: fp16->int6 mse per-dim: [0.03,0.018,0.029,0.001,...].

noah: hypothesis: int6 symmetric quant loses zero-point flexibility for sparse high-value dims. try asymmetric per-channel if you didn't, or hybrid scheme: keep top-4 sensitive channels at fp16 and quantize rest to int6.

jamie: current run was perchannel_asym already. i can try hybrid (per-dim fallback). write command:```bash
python quantize/convert.py --model morlisk-v2 --quant int6 --override-fp16-channels 0,2,5,9 --out morlisk-hybrid.pt
python eval/recall.py --model morlisk-hybrid --holdout wiki-short.csv --k 1 --batch 64
```

ops-bot: note: hybrid fallback increases memory for embeddings table. expect ~+4% RAM.

ci-bot: run 87322 complete. metrics: recall@1 hybrid=0.65, recall@5=0.80, cluster-purity=0.76. centroid-distance-mean delta vs fp16 ~0.011. regression mostly recovered.

saira: nice. hybrid saved the day. seems top dims were bottleneck. can we automate detection of "sensitive channels" in the onboarding pipeline and recommend hybrid fallback for morlisk-v2? also add a small penalty estimate (RAM and small CPU) to the onboarding page.

noah: also add a unit test that fails the quantization job if recall@1 delta > 0.05 on shorttitle cohort unless hybrid/fine-tune applied.

jamie: will add to onboarding doc + PR to eval harness. created ticket INF-7302 for automated detection + unit-test. linked runs: runs/morlisk_int6_1.json, runs/morlisk_hybrid.json.

saira: one more follow-up: we should validate multilingual title holdouts (FR/DE) — token distributions differ and channel sensitivity might change. adding to INF-7302.

noah: thanks. marking thread as actioned. :white_check_mark:
